transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

The most common cause for a machine that fills and drains but won't spin is a broken drive belt, which is very cheap to replace. To confirm this, please unplug the machine, pull it away from the wall, remove the back panel, and check if the belt is still on the drum or has snapped. Let me know what you find.

Right, I've had the back panel off and the belt is still on the pulleys and feels tight, so it hasn't snapped. I did also notice a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, though not since. What would you suggest I look at next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because there was a burning hazard involved, for your safety you must not use the machine again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. However, if the issue is simply worn carbon brushes in the motor, that is much cheaper. To help me give you a more precise idea, could you read me the full model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I've looked at the label inside the door and it reads IWC 71252. I can't make out anything more than that. I've unplugged the machine as you suggested.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Since the belt is intact but the drum won't turn—and you had that hot electrical smell earlier—the most likely culprit is worn-out carbon brushes inside the motor. These are small graphite blocks that wear down over time; when they get too short, the motor can no longer drive the drum and can sometimes produce a burning smell from sparking. With the machine unplugged, could you remove the two small plastic covers on the back of the motor (usually held by one screw each) and check if the carbon brushes are still long enough to spring out? If they are very short or broken off, that is your fault. However, please remember: because there was a burning smell involved, you must not use this machine again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer.
I've got the brushes out of the motor. One is very short and blackened at the tip, as if it's been charred, and the other is a bit longer. Does that sound like the problem?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, that suggests the problem: one brush is worn down to nothing and has been sparking (which caused the blackening and smell), while the other hasn't lasted long enough to wear out. This explains why the drum won't turn. Because there was a burning electrical smell and visible charring, you must not use this machine again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. While replacing the brushes is cheap, the heat from the sparking may have damaged the motor wiring or connections, which needs professional inspection to ensure it is safe. Given the age of the machine (9 years) and the need for an engineer visit, you should weigh that cost against buying a new appliance.
